title: The Thornwall Dinner
sceneText:
Thornwall is larger than Maplegate, and older. There is a dark growth of lichen on the stone, and plainly nobody intends to clean it off; cleaning it off would concede that it is dirt.

The servant showing you in walks half a step behind you and keeps exactly that distance.

There are people in the receiving room already. Baron Henk of Millridge is talking to two other landholders, and his is the loudest voice in the room. Seeing you, he raises a hand at once, as though you had known each other a long time.

“The new steward at Maplegate.” He comes over quickly. “I had heard. Ludwig does move fast.”

An old woman with silver-grey hair is sitting in the seat by the window. She does not rise and she does not speak. She only turns her eyes over.

The volume in the room drops a step.

“Marguerite,” she says. “You are welcome in my house.”

Master Lorenz is here too, standing by the fireplace with a glass in his hand that he has barely touched. He gives you a nod. His position in this room is a delicate one: everybody respects him, and nobody counts him as one of the company.

There are seven places laid at the long table. Yours is the third on Marguerite’s right.

Not the guest of honour. Not the foot of the table.

Sitting down, you understand that the place was chosen. They have not yet decided who you are.

The first course is local: roast roots with mutton, served in deep earthenware, not silver. Marguerite could perfectly well have put out silver. She has not.

“Speaking of timber,” Henk says, turning to you suddenly before the second course, “I have an idea.”

“Maplegate’s woodland is on the north slope. Getting it out means going round the whole line of hills; by your own road that is the better part of a day. By mine it is two hours, and my road was resurfaced this year.” He talks fast. “Hand the timber to me, I will get it to Valehold for you, we price it at market, and we split the difference above it. What you save is time, and time is the thing you are shortest of.”

He is not wrong. Time is exactly what you are shortest of.

The table goes quiet for a moment.

choices.text: That sounds like good value. We could try it

effects.logEntry: You accepted Henk’s timber proposal on the spot at the dinner.

choices.text: Forgive me, but I do not think handing the estate’s timber to a neighbour is sound

effects.logEntry: You refused Henk’s timber proposal in front of the table.

choices.text: I shall have to see how much of this year’s allowance is left, and answer you then

effects.logEntry: You put off answering Henk until you had the figures.
